assurance.title: Exam-ready — including the part that is not ready
assurance.lead: Each figure carries whether it is current, validated and traceable. The Howard University coverage gap is flagged rather than smoothed over, because a number you cannot defend to an examiner is worse than no number at all — and a SAR narrative without lineage is worse still.

options.note: Three paths to bend the curve. One is recommended.
options.note2: These options are not mutually exclusive. The recommended path pairs the targeted member warning and the transfer step-up with closing the Howard University coverage gap — contain the campaign now, and remove the blind spot it is exploiting.

options.title: Targeted warning and transfer step-up
options.desc: Warn the impacted segment in the exact language of the pattern, and step up verification on the transfer patterns the campaign uses. Scoped to the attack path, so most members feel nothing.

options.title: Blanket transfer hold above a threshold
options.desc: Hold every outbound transfer over a threshold for manual review until the campaign passes. Contains fastest, but the friction lands on every member making a legitimate transfer and a lean team clears the backlog.

options.title: Close the coverage gap first
options.desc: Bring the Howard University book into fraud-model scope before acting on the campaign. Removes the blind spot permanently, but the mapping work takes days the campaign does not give you.

nextSteps.note: Each item has an owner set and a response timeframe. Owners are roles, not named individuals — the ESFCU risk roster is an open follow-up.

steps.desc: The warning goes to the impacted segment in the language of the pattern in play, aligned to ESFCU's published fraud guidance so members see one consistent message. The step-up is scoped to the campaign's transfer patterns, not to all transfers.

steps.title: Bring the Howard University book into fraud-model scope
steps.desc: 11,240 accounts to map into the model's account master. Until that lands, coverage is cited as 88% and never as a whole-book figure — including to the supervisory committee and to an examiner.

closing.signoff: The exposure is containable and the response is drafted. What changed is that you can see the campaign, prove every figure, and show the one gap honestly — in the same session.

steps.title: Send the targeted member warning and step up transfers
steps.body: Member Communications own the warning with Digital Banking on the step-up. The warning names the exact impersonation pattern rather than giving generic fraud advice, and it is aligned to ESFCU's published guidance so members are not receiving two competing messages. The step-up is scoped to the campaign's transfer patterns: the friction lands on the attack path, not on the membership.

steps.title: Hold the mule cluster and file the two SARs due this week
steps.body: Fraud Operations place the holds on all 14 flagged accounts; the BSA Officer files SAR-0412 and SAR-0409, which fall due inside seven days. Both narratives are drafted with the evidence attached and the lineage for every figure they cite, which is what makes them defensible to an examiner reading them cold rather than merely complete.

steps.title: Bring the Howard University book into fraud-model scope
steps.body: Risk Technology and Data Governance map the 11,240 division accounts into the model's account master. This is the item dragging exam readiness, and it is the blind spot the campaign is exploiting. Until it lands, coverage is cited as 88% and never as a whole-book figure — to the supervisory committee or to an examiner.
